themes.title: Transnational Recalibration Following MAGA Midterm Defeats
themes.blurb: Right-wing parties across Europe and South America are actively processing the political fallout of the US Republican midterm losses. Factions within the AfD, Reform UK, Lega, and Bolsonarismo are either distancing themselves from Donald Trump's foreign policy or re-evaluating their own electoral vulnerabilities in light of the MAGA defeat.

themes.title: Transnational Right-Wing Networking and Parallel Diplomacy
themes.blurb: Far-right and nationalist leaders are aggressively pursuing cross-border alliances and parallel diplomatic engagements to project international stature. From Javier Milei's high-profile appearance alongside Vox in Madrid to Flávio Bolsonaro's Mar-a-Lago outreach and Marine Le Pen's briefing of European ambassadors, right-wing movements are strengthening transnational links.

themes.title: Judicial Crackdowns and Surveillance Targeting the Far-Right
themes.blurb: Right-wing parties in multiple democracies are facing expanding state surveillance, judicial proceedings, and constitutional bans. In Germany, interior officials are reviewing hundreds of thousands of AfD emails for party ban proceedings, while in Poland, Brazil, and France, far-right leaders face active court battles, electoral disqualification threats, and judicial scrutiny.

themes.title: Far-Right Momentum and Electoral Contestation Ahead of Major Votes
themes.blurb: Far-right parties across Northern and Southern Europe are adjusting coalition tactics and escalating pre-campaign momentum. In Sweden, SD drops cabinet demands to maneuver center-right partners into power, while Vox in Spain, AfD in Germany, and FrP in Norway capitalize on strong polling to challenge mainstream conservative dominance.
